idiom_name: for { x <- mx } yield f(x) - flatMap/map/withFilter desugaring
implementation_notes: The compiler rewrites a for-comprehension into flatMap for each generator, map for the yield and withFilter for guards; any type providing those methods (Option, Either, Try, Future, List, IO) becomes a monad with comprehension syntax, which is the pattern absorbed into the language. Use the comprehension form for the value-level chain; reach for cats-effect when the effect needs a runtime (cancellation, resource safety, tracing).
pitfalls: The desugaring fixes the container type of the first generator, so mixing effects inside one comprehension (Future and Option) requires EitherT/OptionT transformers.
Guards become withFilter, which for Future and IO is not lazy the way people expect, and a refutable pattern in a generator can throw instead of short-circuiting.
A for-comprehension that only maps still calls flatMap on the first generator unless written with a single generator and no extra bindings, which surprises newcomers profiling hot paths.

variants.name: cats-effect IO values (description + runtime)
variants.idiom_name: cats.effect.IO with flatMap/for-comprehension, run at the edge
variants.implementation_notes: cats-effect makes the IO instance first-class: an IO[A] is a lazy description that can be pure, async, blocking or cancelable, flatMap chains dependent steps (short-circuiting failures because IO is a MonadError) and the runtime interprets the value with unsafeRunSync/unsafeRunAsync. Program logic stays pure and testable and the interpreter is chosen at main; use it when the application needs resource safety and cancellation, not merely chaining.
pitfalls: Nothing runs until the IO is interpreted: a value built and never run is a silent no-op, and side effects must live in delay/blocking/async.
Resources need Resource/bracket; manual acquire/release inside a flatMap chain leaks when the chain is cancelled.
IO's errors are untyped by default (Throwable); EitherT/IO[Either[E, A]] is required when the failure type is part of the contract.
